assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window is what I value most. The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the later association with a flaring blazar, created neutrino astronomy as a working field. It rests on a very large detector, careful background rejection and years of calibration.
assessment.attribution: Only one name is credited, and I would expect that to be the proposer and long-time leader of the IceCube concept and collaboration. A fair prize may need others, for instance the pioneers of the technique or the collaboration leadership, but those people are not in the supplied credit, so I can only propose the one name.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed in several channels and energy ranges with growing significance. The Galactic-plane result and the blazar and Seyfert source evidence add support. The detector has been running for over a decade, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether a single-laureate configuration is adequate given the size of the collaboration and the earlier pioneers is unresolved.
The identification of the main source classes is still incomplete, though the existence of the flux is secure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene gave a clean, tunable platform for correlated insulators and superconductivity, and it created the whole field of twistronics. The discovery is original and the impact is broad. It follows a theory prediction by an experiment that proved it.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero group's 2018 correlated-insulator and superconductivity experiments are the decisive steps. Eva Andrei's group made important independent observations, so the configuration is a hard choice. Condensed matter is outside my own expertise and I would rely on colleagues here.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced the main phenomena, and the field has spread to other moire systems. Understanding of the superconducting pairing mechanism is still immature, but the discovery of the flat bands and correlated states is firm.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled.
The allocation among Andrei, Jarillo-Herrero and the theorists is disputed, and a three-person limit excludes someone with a strong claim.
This is outside my expertise, so my judgment of the credit rests on the supplied text and general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect were a conceptual shift in how we classify electronic matter, with a prediction followed by experimental realization. The idea has had lasting influence on materials, spintronics and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theory, and Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Hasan's ARPES work on three-dimensional topological insulators is also strong. The list includes four names, and the BHZ proposers are not in the credit, so any trio leaves an open question.
assessment.maturity: The effect has been confirmed many times in several materials, and the theory is well established. The recognition is not premature, and arguably it is overdue.
uncertainties: Credit among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp and Hasan, and the missing theory proposers, is unresolved.
I rely on condensed-matter colleagues for the finer points of attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a nonzero theta13 mixing angle was a decisive measurement that opened the way to CP violation searches in the lepton sector. It was a precise and clean reactor-neutrino experiment, which I like as an experimentalist.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay under Yifang Wang, with Kam-Biu Luk as co-spokesperson, made the first precise reactor measurement. Nishikawa led T2K, which observed electron-neutrino appearance, so the credit between reactor and accelerator results is not trivial. The pair for Daya Bay is my best fit, but Double Chooz and RENO also reported independently.
assessment.maturity: Several independent experiments confirmed the result within a year, and it has been refined since. The neutrino-oscillation theme was already recognized in 2002 and 2015, and this is a distinct and lasting discovery.
uncertainties: The relative claims of Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K are not entirely settled in the supplied credit.
The scientific importance depends partly on later CP-violation findings, which are still open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localization of gamma-ray burst afterglows with BeppoSAX, followed by optical redshifts, settled the long debate about the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts. It was an instrument-driven breakthrough in my own field and gave a new class of cosmological probe.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX Wide Field Camera and gamma-ray burst monitor results that gave arcminute positions in 1997. Kulkarni's group provided important follow-up redshifts, but others such as van Paradijs, Djorgovski and Paczynski also contributed and are not in the list. I would be cautious about the allocation.
assessment.maturity: The cosmological origin is secure and has been confirmed by decades of observations with Swift, Fermi and others. Recognition is long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Many people contributed to the optical and radio follow-up, and the supplied credit is incomplete for them.
Some of the main contributors have died, which constrains the possible configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, using the magic-wavelength idea, brought fractional uncertainties at the 1e-18 level and are redefining timekeeping and precision tests. It is a clear instrument advance that opens new measurements, from geodesy to tests of fundamental constants.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and built the first one. Jun Ye's group pushed it to the best accuracy and stability. The two-name credit looks coherent, but ion clocks and the frequency comb work, already recognized in 2005, are related.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation exists from many labs, and the clocks are the basis for the planned redefinition of the second. The recognition would be timely, though the redefinition itself is still pending.
uncertainties: It overlaps in people and ideas with earlier prizes on frequency combs and ion traps, and the committee would need to define the novelty clearly.
I rely on atomic-physics colleagues for the technical details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in galaxy clustering gave a standard ruler that is a pillar of precision cosmology and of dark-energy constraints. It is observationally clean and has been tested in many surveys.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections were made by SDSS, led by Eisenstein, and 2dFGRS, led by Cole and Percival, so the two independent detections are fairly represented. The theory of the acoustic peak goes back to Peebles, Yu and Sunyaev, Zeldovich and others, who are not in the credit, which is a complication.
assessment.maturity: Many independent surveys, up to BOSS and DESI, confirm it, and the standard-ruler interpretation is robust. Recent DESI hints about evolving dark energy show it is still an active frontier, but that does not undermine the detection.
uncertainties: Prior theoretical work, and the large survey collaborations, make the allocation of credit hard.
The relation to recent evolving dark-energy claims is not yet settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new part of the gravitational-wave spectrum, a landmark for experimental astrophysics that was built on decades of pulsar timing and calibration.
assessment.attribution: The pulsar-timing array work of NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA and others is collective. Manchester, Kramer and McLaughlin are leaders of different arrays, but the 2023 evidence was found by several collaborations, so the choice of three is arbitrary to some extent.
assessment.maturity: This is the least mature on my list. Signals are around the 3 to 4 sigma level, the spectrum amplitude is somewhat larger than expected, and the origin as supermassive black hole binaries is not confirmed. A prize might be premature until a Hellings-Downs detection is firmer and the source is clear.
uncertainties: The significance is below the 5 sigma discovery standard in most analyses.
The astrophysical or cosmological origin is not established.
Credit is spread over several collaborations, and three names cannot represent them fairly.
